posts.title: Glossary: Hucclecote to Kitesnest
posts.description: It’s not a new book or even a new idea, but my own little book: Glossary is a diversion, hopefully not a contraflow. It’s available on Amazon, and briefly, it is a collection of Gloucestershire place names given new meanings by me. I am publishing some selected pages here over the next few weeks. If you would like a copy of the entire collection, you can find it on Amazon. Search for Glossary by Paul Davies. I suppose this is my version of sharing a joke. For the uninitiated, it is a great pastime when travelling: to give new meanings to place names. Try it! Hucclecote One of those parkas your dad or granddad used to own in the 70s that you never bothered to throw away. The undefined fur on the collar is somewhat perished and moth-eaten. posts.title: Glossary: Hatherley to Hawkesbury Upton
posts.description: It’s not a new book or even a new idea, but my own little book: Glossary is a diversion, hopefully not a contraflow. It’s available on Amazon, and briefly, it is a collection of Gloucestershire place names given new meanings by me. I am publishing some selected pages here over the next few weeks. If you would like a copy of the entire collection, you can find it on Amazon; just search Glossary by Paul Davies. I suppose this is my version of sharing a joke. For the uninitiated, it is a great pastime when travelling: to give new meanings to place names. Try it! Hatherley Wet washing that won’t dry, no matter what the weather. Eventually gives off a strange odour like a wet dog. Hatherop Male surgical procedure in an unspeakable place. Haresfield A field with a hare in it. This is an increasingly rare event, so these days Haresfield can mean rare. Hardwicke Poor light conditions. Derived from pre-electricity days.
